# The step of a dot product of one limb: one fused multiply-add

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `dot_step_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$s + x y$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y).$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_conv_1`, called by `convolution`, the product of polynomials, of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y)$: the number of the format nearest to $s + x y$, ties to even.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `dot_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/StepKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/StepKernels.v), against `dot_step_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions dot_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition dot_step_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s x y : R,
  fmt emin prec s ->
  fmt emin prec x ->
  fmt emin prec y ->
  let t := dot_step_1 emin prec tie_even s x y in
  fmt emin prec t /\
  t = RN emin prec (s + (x * y)).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `dot_step_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the step of the fused dot product of one limb, s <- RN(x y + s) (milestone2.md). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/dot_step_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/dot_step_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The step of the dot product of one limb (milestone2.md, "sum, dot, axpy, convolution"): one
# fused operation, s <- RN(x y + s). No product is rounded: the step is the addition of the state
# and of the exact product. Its elements come from arrays the program supplies; it only multiplies
# them, so rule R3 asks no guard of them (an entry kernel whose x and y enter from the program).

t = fma(x, y, s)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
